guitar.notes: Ted Nugent's Gibson Byrdland is well documented as his signature stage instrument, distinctive among rock guitarists of his era.

tone.target: dirty hot-rodded Marshall crunch with biting mids
tone.profile: dirty hot-rodded Marshall crunch with biting mids
tone.summary: A classic British stack simulation (UK 45/UK Vintage 4x12) with a Boost for aggressive riffing, Distortion for core grit, and an occasional Wah accent. The focus is on tight, biting mids characteristic of early 80s hard rock.

rig.name: Ted Nugent - Cat Scratch Fever - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum inherent in aggressive riffing.
Provide aggressive edge and tighten the attack for riffing.
Establish the core 'dirty hot-rodded' crunch and grit.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated Marshall model, so general Distortion is used to simulate the necessary mid-punch without modern saturation.

blocks.purpose: Occasional wah accent for lead lines and solos.
Simulate the classic British Marshall stack tone and biting mids.
Provide the necessary British cabinet voicing and punch.
Boost the mid-punch and cut unnecessary low end to maintain tightness.
Used sparingly for lead lines to add dimension without heavy modulation.
blocks.gap: The target tone avoids heavy modulation, so this is kept optional and subtle.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle depth and sustain to lead passages.
Provide a natural sense of space without muddying the aggressive tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and punch by swapping the current IR for a more aggressive, mid-focused 4x12.

proposals.reason: Enhance punch and grit matching the hard rock era tone.
